name: Closed Sicilian
summary: The Closed Sicilian (2.Nc3, g3, Bg2) sidesteps open theory, fianchettoing and storming the kingside with f4-f5.
intro: The Closed Sicilian arises after 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7, when White declines to open the centre with an early d4 and instead builds a slow, systematic attack. White fianchettoes the king's bishop, castles, and prepares the kingside pawn advance f4-f5, while Black mirrors the set-up and expands on the opposite wing. It is a strategic, manoeuvring battle that lets White avoid the vast theory of the Open Sicilian.
line: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The defining choice of the Closed Sicilian is that White keeps the centre closed rather than playing d4 to open lines. By fianchettoing with g3 and Bg2 and holding the pawns on e4 and d3, White sets up a durable structure and postpones any concrete confrontation. The plan is thematic and easy to remember: complete development with Nf3 or Nge2, castle short, and then roll the kingside pawns forward with f4, sometimes supported by g4 and h4, aiming for the space-gaining break f5.

Both sides typically expand on the flank where they are strongest. White plays on the kingside towards Black's king, while Black seeks queenside counterplay with ...b5, ...b4 and pressure down the half-open c-file, often supported by ...Rb8 and ...a5. Because the centre stays fixed for long stretches, understanding of pawn breaks and piece manoeuvres matters more than memorised lines, and the side that arrives first with a well-prepared attack usually seizes the initiative.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: The classical main line runs 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.d3 d6, after which White continues developing with Be3, Qd2 and Nge2, keeping the knight off f3 so the f-pawn can advance unobstructed. White then plays f4 and prepares f5, while castling short and reserving the option of expanding further with g4 and h4. Black, meanwhile, builds queenside play with ...Rb8, ...b5 and ...b4 to dislodge the c3-knight and open lines against White's king.

White has flexible move orders and can choose the placement of the king's knight, since Nge2 supports the f4-f5 plan whereas Nf3 leads to quieter, more positional handling. Related to the Closed Sicilian is the Grand Prix Attack, in which White plays an early f4 (frequently 2.Nc3 followed by 3.f4) for a more direct assault on the kingside. Black's principal antidote in all these lines is rapid queenside counterplay, meeting White's kingside ambitions with sharp play of his own before the attack becomes dangerous.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The Closed Sicilian has long appealed to players who prefer strategy and understanding to the memorisation demanded by the Open Sicilian. It was handled with great artistry by Vasily Smyslov and became strongly associated with Boris Spassky, who scored a number of memorable attacking victories with it at the highest level. Its enduring popularity among club players and grandmasters alike stems from its clear plans and its usefulness as a practical way to steer the game into calmer, self-directed channels.

keyIdeas: White keeps the centre closed, declining the early d4 of the Open Sicilian.
The fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 supports a slow build-up and kingside pawn storm.
White's main plan is f4 and f5, often backed by g4 and h4.
Black seeks queenside counterplay with ...b5, ...b4 and pressure on the c-file.
Nge2 keeps the f-pawn's path clear, unlike the more positional Nf3.
It is a manoeuvring, understanding-based system that avoids heavy Open Sicilian theory.

white: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, then castle short behind a solid centre.
Advance f4 and prepare the space-gaining break f5, adding g4 and h4 when possible.
Develop with d3, Be3, Qd2 and Nge2 to keep the f-pawn's path clear.
Aim the pieces at Black's king and open lines on the kingside.
Consider the Grand Prix Attack with an early f4 for a more direct assault.
black: Mirror White's fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7 and complete development.
Expand on the queenside with ...Rb8, ...b5 and ...b4 to hit the c3-knight.
Use the half-open c-file to pressure White's queenside.
React to f5 accurately, either exchanging or blocking to blunt the attack.
Race for counterplay before White's kingside pawn storm gathers force.
